features.description: harness gc reaps the tmux sessions of ended, dead-driver, unpaused runs of its project and the queue runner does the same across projects before the debrief, through one shared helper that never touches h-queue, the desk or a live run.
steps: One helper (as the plan fixed) reaps run → tmux_name sessions where <state>/ended exists, driver.pid is not alive (re-checked just before the kill) and PAUSE is absent, logging `+ reaped tmux session <s> (<run> ended)`; cmd_gc calls it for its project through act (`would:` on --dry-run) and goes on after a failed kill

A check on the private server: sessions h-<ended run>, h-queue, $HARNESS_DESK_SESSION, h-<live-driver run> (a run whose driver.pid names the suite's own shell) and h-<paused run> (PAUSE marker, no ended) exist; `harness gc proj` kills only the ended run's session and the other four survive; a second ended run's session is also reaped in the same gc (one reap doesn't stop the rest)
A check: `harness gc proj --dry-run` prints `would: ... kill-session` and every session still exists

lib/queue.sh calls the same helper for every project as it exits, before the debrief line; a check on the existing queue-runner test: no h-<run> session remains for a run the runner started that has ended, and h-queue and the desk session are untouched

features.description: gc's worktree removal finishes: a clean tree with ignored build output is removed with --force then rm -rf, a failure is logged as `! could not remove <wt>: <why>` and the next worktree is still processed.
steps: cmd_gc removes a clean, merged worktree with `git worktree remove --force`, then `rm -rf` if the directory remains, then `git worktree prune`; a failure prints `! could not remove <wt>: <why>` and the loop continues
A check: two merged, clean worktrees in list order, the first holding a gitignored .next/ directory with a file in it; `harness gc proj` removes both and prints `+` lines for both

A check: a worktree whose removal fails (its directory made read-only by its parent's mode, restored after) prints the `! could not remove` line and the worktree after it is still removed; `--dry-run` removes nothing and prints `would:` for each

features.description: harness gc --deps deletes DEPS_DIRS (node_modules .next .next-check .venv) inside the worktrees of ended runs, even unmerged ones, logging the space freed, and never inside a live run's worktree or the project's own checkout.
steps: lib/config.sh defaults DEPS_DIRS="node_modules .next .next-check .venv" (templates/user/config.sh commented); cmd_gc takes --deps and, for each worktree under $WT_ROOT/<project>/ whose run has ended, has no live driver.pid, no queued continuation and no open desk, deletes each named directory that exists and prints `+ freed <n> MB in <wt>: <dirs>` (du -sm before deleting)

A check: an ended, unmerged run's worktree holding node_modules/x.js and .venv/y is emptied of both by `harness gc proj --deps` while its branch and every committed file remain; a live run's worktree (driver.pid naming the suite's shell) keeps its node_modules; the project checkout $T/proj keeps a node_modules placed there; `--dry-run --deps` deletes nothing and prints `would: freed`
A check: a run with a queued continuation (an entry in $HARNESS_STATE/queue/*-continue-<run>.args) keeps its directories

features.description: The queue runner runs `harness gc <project> --all-merged --deps` for every project it started a run in, before the debrief, its output in runner.log, and a gc failure never stops the debrief.
steps: lib/queue.sh, on its exit path when it started runs, collects the distinct projects of those runs (from <state>/runners matching its id) and runs `harness gc <project> --all-merged --deps` for each, with `gc <project>:` prefixed lines in runner.log, before the debrief line; a non-zero gc exit logs `gc <project> failed (exit <n>)` and the debrief still starts
